case_title: Pooranlal & Anr. v. The State of Madhya Pradesh
high_court_outcome: Confined the acquittal of three accused, but convicted the appellants-accused u!s. 304 (Part II) rw s.34
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The prosecution case against the accused and other three individuals involved an incident where the deceased, Hariya, was assaulted with lathis by five persons. The deceased was taken to a police station and lodged an FIR. He was later admitted to a hospital where he sustained multiple injuries. The deceased survived for 14 days after the incident and eventually succumbed to his injuries. The post-mortem examination did not establish that the injuries were sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death. The prosecution argued that the accused, including the appellants, were involved in the assault, and that there was no motive to kill the deceased, but rather to teach a lesson for past insults. The trial court acquitted all accused, but the High Court reversed the acquittal of the appellants and convicted them under Section 304 Part II read with Section 34 IPC.
